summary.headline: Akums Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13.9% YoY to INR1,167 crore and EBITDA 35.4% to INR175 crore, led by CDMO volumes and API prices.
summary.overview: Operating revenue reached INR1,167 crore (+13.9% YoY, +0.8% QoQ) and operating EBITDA INR175 crore (+35.4% YoY), with margin at 15.0%, up 238 bps YoY. PAT rose 56.1% YoY to INR101 crore. CDMO carried the quarter with 18.6% revenue growth and higher capacity utilisation, while domestic branded (Akumentis) and international branded formulations were muted on EBITDA, the former due to a ~200-person field force addition. Management reiterated 14-15% annual margin guidance and said it could lean to the upper end, and announced the Oriflame India manufacturing acquisition.

financial_highlights.change: +13.9% YoY; +0.8% QoQ vs Q4 FY26 INR1,158 crore
+35.4% YoY; margin +238 bps YoY, up from 13.1% in Q4 FY26
+56.1% YoY; +24.1% QoQ vs Q4 FY26 INR81 crore
Management stated no debt; net worth above INR3,400 crore

segments.name: CDMO
segments.commentary: Revenue INR964 crore (+18.6% YoY, +1.3% QoQ) on volume growth and higher API prices; EBITDA INR163 crore (+36.8% YoY), aided by better capacity utilisation.

segments.name: Domestic branded formulations (Akumentis)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR115 crore (+7.3% YoY, +12.9% QoQ); EBITDA INR12 crore (-25.4% YoY, -46.5% QoQ) due to field force expansion of ~200 people (~15%).

segments.name: International branded formulations
segments.commentary: Revenue INR35 crore (-1.5% YoY, -3.6% QoQ); EBITDA INR6.9 crore (-14.4% YoY, -31.4% QoQ).

segments.name: API
segments.commentary: Revenue INR32 crore (-29.7% YoY, -22.3% QoQ); EBITDA minus INR4 crore vs minus INR6 crore in Q1 FY26 and minus INR12 crore in Q4 FY26, helped by non-cepha mix; COGS down to about 75% from about 90%+.

segments.name: Trade generics
segments.commentary: Revenue INR21 crore (-9.5% YoY, -23.4% QoQ); EBITDA around breakeven (INR0.1 crore) for second straight quarter vs minus INR5 crore a year ago.

guidance_outlook: CDMO volume growth expected in high teens in Q2 FY27; management says volume growth will at least be double digit in coming quarters.
Annual EBITDA margin guided at 14-15%, with management inclining to the upper end given strong Q1.

Zambia: about USD 25 million (roughly INR240 crore) revenue targeted in FY27, with revenue recognition from Q3 and some of Q4; over 100 products agreed with the Zambian government; similar scale expected next fiscal.
Zambia and Europe margins expected to be similar to or higher than current CDMO margins (higher teens). European business to start in the next fiscal year.
API: monthly EBITDA-positive target by end of February/March 2027; annual profitability from FY28.
Domestic branded formulations: price increase already taken, to reflect from the current quarter; management expects better performance from Q3 onwards.
Baddi oral facility expected to go live near the end of FY27; capex not yet disclosed.
capex_capacity: Utilisation at about 50%+; management says peak utilisation can reach 55-60%.
New oral manufacturing facility at Baddi expected to go live near the end of FY27; capex amount still under discussion.

Acquired Oriflame India's manufacturing business (announced 23 July 2026): plants at Roorkee (Uttarakhand) and Noida (UP), plus a leased Noida warehouse; expands skin care, cosmetics and colour cosmetics capacity. Plant 5 is dedicated to cosmeceuticals and was near peak utilisation.
No subcontracting planned; management says low-margin portfolio will not be rationalised as gross margins remain above 40%.
demand_pricing: CDMO volume growth high teens in Q3 FY26, Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27; IPM volume growth cited at about 2-3%.
API prices rising since February-March 2026 and still volatile; management says Q2 prices trending up.
Cost-plus pricing model: input cost changes are passed through on each purchase order.
CDMO gross margin improvement attributed mainly to high-value products; inventory gains described as very limited. Management says the gross margin level is sustainable plus or minus 0.5%.
Domestic growth in Akumentis from a mix of new launches, price and volume; management did not quantify the split.
Unosource (international) muted in Q1; management expects order growth from Q2-Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a time frame to evaluate exiting the API business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not a question of a U-turn; the focus is on improving profitability, with quarterly losses declining over the past two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Zambia timing and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue expected from Q3 and some of Q4; about USD 25 million (roughly INR240 crore) in FY27; margins expected in the higher teens.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net cash figure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed about INR1,600 crore is net of debt; 98% is in fixed deposits with nationalised banks.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Oriflame deal capability or capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described it as a niche formulation play that adds skin care capacity and enables entry into colour cosmetics, building on R&D strength.

qa_highlights.question: Why is domestic sales-force productivity below industry and why add MRs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company is in a build phase, with the MR addition targeting new geographies and headquarters, and that productivity will rise toward industry averages as the business scales.

risks_watch: Akumentis EBITDA fell to INR12 crore (-46.5% QoQ) as field force expansion weighs on margin; watch for recovery from Q3.
International branded formulations and Unosource muted; EBITDA down 14.4% YoY.
Q1 margin partly helped by API price rise and Q4 inventory build, so sustainability of 15% margin depends on API price trends.
API segment still EBITDA-negative (INR-4 crore); monthly breakeven target by Feb-Mar 2027 to monitor.
Zambia revenue timing has slipped from Q2 to Q3/Q4; ramp-up depends on government contract execution.
Capital deployment of INR1,600 crore cash: no specific M&A or dividend plan disclosed; acquisition size and Oriflame financial contribution not disclosed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on CDMO momentum and FY27 volume and margin outlook, with Q2 described as encouraging. Cautious and vague on specifics: capex for Baddi, Oriflame financials, and cash deployment were not quantified. Defensive when questioned on API strategy, sales-force productivity, and senior talent.
key_quotes: So the management is fully confident, right? So this is a business we have been investing for over 3, 4 years now.
So rightly on both the Zambia as well as Europe, so these will be margins which are similar, maybe that higher than -- in the higher teens compared to our current CDMO business, right?
So there is no concept of subcontracting, honestly.
Most of it is largely through high-value products being getting added.
Most of the money, in fact, 98% of the money is parked in fixed deposits with nationalized banks, right?
So the whole target is on a monthly level, at least by the end of February, March, we should be monthly EBITDA positive in this business.
